skill.name: wiki-vitepress
skill.description: Packages generated wiki Markdown into a dark VitePress static site with Mermaid diagram support, click-to-zoom diagrams, and production build output.
skill.summary: Builds a dark VitePress wiki site from generated Markdown.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, VitePress output paths, and Mermaid terminology. The real issues are the generated click-to-zoom snippet using innerHTML and a standard npm build command with normal dependency-script risk; no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Generated Mermaid zoom code assigns modal.innerHTML from existing diagram markup.
remediation.suggestion: Use cloneNode or a sanitized render path instead of innerHTML when building the zoom modal. Treat Markdown and Mermaid content as untrusted input.

remediation.issue: The build workflow runs npm install and npm package scripts in the generated project.
remediation.suggestion: Pin dependencies, commit a lockfile when possible, and consider npm ci with script restrictions for untrusted projects.

static_findings.snippet: Generate the following structure in a `wiki-site/` directory:
- Configure `themeConfig.nav` and `themeConfig.sidebar` from the catalogue structure
Mermaid inline `style` attributes override everything. Use `onMounted` + polling to replace them:
Use `setup()` with `onMounted`, NOT `enhanceApp()` — DOM doesn't exist during SSR.
Wrap each `.mermaid` container in a clickable wrapper that opens a fullscreen modal:
Before VitePress build, scan all `.md` files and fix:
- Wrap bare `<T>` generic parameters in backticks outside code fences
- Ensure every page has YAML frontmatter with `title` and `description`
- Mermaid renders async — SVGs don't exist when `onMounted` fires. Must poll.
- `isCustomElement` compiler option for bare `<T>` causes worse crashes — do NOT use it
- Node text in Mermaid uses inline `style` with highest specificity — CSS alone won't fix it
- `enhanceApp()` runs during SSR where `document` doesn't exist — use `setup()` only

medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The theme snippet assigns modal.innerHTML from el.outerHTML. Mermaid or wiki content can be input-derived, so cloning markup through innerHTML can preserve unsafe HTML or event attributes in the generated site.

medium_findings.title: Ruby/shell backtick execution

content.value_statement: Generated wiki Markdown can be hard to browse and share. This skill packages it into a dark VitePress site with Mermaid support.
actual_capabilities: Scaffolds a wiki-site directory with VitePress configuration and theme files.
Configures vitepress-plugin-mermaid with dark theme variables for diagrams.
Adds CSS overrides and mounted DOM fixes for Mermaid inline styles.
Creates click-to-zoom behavior for Mermaid diagrams in the generated site.
Defines Markdown post-processing rules for line breaks, generic type text, and frontmatter.
Builds production output into the VitePress dist directory.
limitations: It assumes generated Markdown pages already exist before packaging starts.
It targets a dark-only VitePress presentation rather than a full theme system.
It requires Node.js and npm to install dependencies and build the site.
Generated client-side snippets need review before publishing untrusted content.

use_cases.title: Publish Generated Project Wikis
use_cases.description: Turn generated Markdown pages into a browsable static documentation site with navigation and sidebar structure.

use_cases.title: Share AI Research Notes
use_cases.description: Package deep wiki output into a site that teammates can open, search, and review in a browser.

use_cases.title: Render Diagram-Heavy Docs
use_cases.description: Improve Mermaid diagram visibility with dark styling and click-to-zoom behavior for architecture pages.

prompt_templates.title: Package A Basic Wiki
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for an existing Markdown wiki folder.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a VitePress wiki site from my generated Markdown pages. Use the default dark theme and create production output.

prompt_templates.title: Add Mermaid Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Package these wiki pages as VitePress and configure Mermaid diagrams for dark mode with readable text and edges.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare A Shareable Build
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a ready-to-host documentation artifact.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the wiki-site structure, add navigation from the catalogue, post-process Markdown issues, and build the static site.

prompt_templates.title: Customize Diagram Experience
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a polished site with interactive diagram viewing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a VitePress wiki with dark Mermaid styling, inline style correction, and click-to-zoom diagrams. Review unsafe DOM patterns before finalizing.

output_examples.input: A folder of generated wiki Markdown pages and a page catalogue.
output_examples.output: A wiki-site project with VitePress configuration, theme files, navigation, sidebar entries, and copied Markdown pages.

output_examples.input: Architecture documentation that includes Mermaid diagrams.
output_examples.output: A dark documentation site where Mermaid diagrams use readable colors and can open in a fullscreen zoom view.

output_examples.input: Markdown pages with missing frontmatter and VitePress compatibility issues.
output_examples.output: Pages prepared with titles, descriptions, compatible line breaks, and escaped generic type text.

best_practices: Review generated Markdown before publishing it to a public site.
Pin VitePress and plugin dependencies when creating a repeatable build.
Test Mermaid diagrams after the production build, not only during local preview.
anti_patterns: Do not use the generated site as a replacement for source documentation review.
Do not publish untrusted Markdown without checking embedded HTML and diagram content.
Do not skip the VitePress build step when verifying navigation and Mermaid rendering.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates a VitePress wiki site from existing Markdown pages, including theme files, Mermaid settings, and build output.

faq.question: Does it write the wiki content itself?
faq.answer: No. It packages generated Markdown into a browsable site and applies compatibility fixes.

faq.question: Does it support Mermaid diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It configures Mermaid for a dark theme and adds extra styling rules for readability.

faq.question: Can I host the output as a static site?
faq.answer: Yes. The production build creates static files in the VitePress dist directory.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted Markdown?
faq.answer: Untrusted Markdown should be reviewed first, especially embedded HTML and Mermaid content used by client-side diagram features.
